papers.title: Laurent Phenomenon Algebras on Minuscule Grassmannians and their Mirrors
papers.abstract: We construct Laurent phenomenon (LP) seeds whose upper algebras are the homogeneous coordinate rings of the half-spin Grassmannians and the Freudenthal variety. The frozen coordinate lines form a Coxeter orbit and define an anticanonical divisor. For these varieties and for the Cayley plane with the seed of Daisey and Ducat, we identify the Keel--Yu mirror of the affine boundary complement with an explicit upper LP algebra after specializing the curve-class parameters to one. We determine the theta function of each boundary component and hence the superpotential. The half-spin formulas are uniform in the rank. In the exceptional cases we compute the theta functions from contact orders and Laurent divisibility. The mirror identifications hold over the integers, and the intrinsic theta basis is valuatively independent in every reachable seed.

papers.title: Theta Functions and Intrinsic Mirrors of Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We construct bases of upper Laurent phenomenon algebras over a field by minimizing Newton polytopes in a single seed. For any translation-invariant total order on the exponents, each least exponent $a$ that occurs determines a smallest Newton polytope $Q_a$. Choose one element with Newton polytope $Q_a$ and least term $x^a$ for each such $a$. These elements form a basis. In every reachable seed chart, every Gauss valuation takes a nonzero basis expansion to the minimum of its values on the nonzero summands. Suppose the algebra has Laurent coefficients and smooth spectrum over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. After setting the curve parameters to one, we compute theta products on the intrinsic mirror from the exchange polynomials and give a finite presentation of the mirror algebra. A seed has a polynomial corner if each exchange polynomial can be multiplied by a unit of the coefficient ring to give a polynomial with constant term one. At such a corner, order the exponents by a weight with strictly positive, rationally independent coordinates. For every lattice exponent $a$ and integral weight $p$, the theta function indexed by $p$ has least $a$-weight $\min_{b\in Q_a}\langle b,p\rangle$ in the corresponding mirror chart. This reciprocity holds for cyclic exchanges and arbitrary pole orders. For fixed exchange supports and constant terms one, we determine when the mirror is smooth and the second mirror recovers the original algebra in the chosen torus coordinates. The coefficient tuples for which both conditions hold form a computable finite set. All their entries are positive integers.

papers.title: Cycle popping and positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that every monomial in the cluster variables of a linear Laurent phenomenon algebra is a nonnegative combination of cluster monomials, as conjectured by Lam and the second author. The proof uses Wilson's cycle popping. We also give a new proof of Laurent positivity in linear Laurent phenomenon algebras, previously established by the first author.

papers.title: Positive bases and polytopes for Laurent phenomenon algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that the cluster monomials of every graph Laurent phenomenon algebra form an atomic positive basis. For every finite normalized Laurent phenomenon algebra over a unique factorization domain, we construct a simple lattice polytope with unimodular normal fan whose polar realizes the cluster complex. We also prove that cluster monomials form a basis of the upper algebra in the finite case. In particular, every linear Laurent phenomenon algebra admits such a polyhedral realization.

papers.title: Positivity for Weighted Linear Laurent Phenomenon Algebras
papers.abstract: We prove Laurent positivity for ordinary Laurent phenomenon algebras whose initial exchange polynomials are nonconstant affine linear polynomials with positive constant terms and nonnegative numerical coefficients.
